Commentary.Commentary: Right then, that is all we have from this game but there's one more match left. The final T20I and also the final game of this multi-format series will be played on 10th October. That match will start at 6:10 pm local (8:10 am GMT). Do join us for that. Till then, goodbye and take cheers!

PLAYER OF THE MATCH, Tahlia McGrath says that India bowled well and they are happy to win the multi-format series. The Indian bowlers showed how good the wicket was for bowlers and cross-seam deliveries were important. Mentions that it's always special playing for the national side and she enjoys it. Adds that the final match should be a close one as well and they will look to assess the Indian bowlers today and adjust accordingly.

The skipper of India Women, Harmanpreet Kaur says that they were 20 odd runs short. Mentions that the wicket wasn't easy to bat on. Tells that they had a good game and didn't give them easy runs. Tells that they fought till the very end. About Pooja, she says that she has the talent and she gets runs for the team whenever needed. Further says that she knows Australia is a great side and they need to come out with good plans and a good approach against them.

The skipper of Australia Women, Meg Lanning says that they bowled and fielded really well and it was their best fielding performance in the series. Applauds Vastrakar for her innings but still feels that the opponents were 15-20 runs short. Also commends McGrath for her match-winning knock. Adds that it's always good when there is a challenge in front of them and that is what makes players better.

Earlier in the day, after electing to bowl, Australia had India under the mat after at 81 for 9. Pooja Vastrakar though played a blinder down the order. That total never seemed enough but Indian bowlers did a tremendous job. However, Tahlia kept her head, played a brilliant knock, and helped the Aussies take an unassailable 1-0 lead in the three-match T20I series but most importantly win the multi-format series.

Not the best of days for the Australian batters but they needed just two from their long batting line-up to actually play a good innings and Tahlia and Mooney provided it. When wickets were falling, Mooney held fort at one end and she always managed to find a boundary here and there to release the pressure. She along with Tahlia got the chase back on track. Once she fell though, McGrath took the responsibility, she too had wickets falling at the other end but the all-rounder stayed till the end and won her side the game

India Women needed wickets and that is what they got! They had Australia 4 down even before they crossed 50 and also did not let them score freely. Gayakwad was brilliant. Pandey too was really good with the new ball. The others also stuck to their task well. At one stage, they put the pressure back onto Australia but have to say, it was India's fielding that let them down. There could have been a couple of boundaries that could have been stopped, also a few chances which were not taken, and in the end, that cost them the game.

What a game of cricket! Never thought after the first innings, when India just put up 118, this would go down to the wire but the spirit of this Indian side, the never-give-up attitude has seen them make a game out of this. Yes, they did not defend it but have to commend the effort they put in.

That's it, Tahlia McGrath has seen her team through and Australia Women win the multi-format series as well. On off and McGrath gets an inside edge back onto the pads. The ball rolls onto the off side and McGrath scampers through for the winning run. AUSTRALIA WOMEN WIN BY 4 WICKETS!
Back of a length, on middle. McGrath pulls it towards mid-wicket for a single. Scores are level.
On middle and Wareham eases it down to long on for another one. Just 2 needed now.
Full and straight, drilled down to long on for one.
Full toss, on the pads. McGrath flicks it past square leg and picks up a couple.

FOUR! You just can't give any width to Tahlia McGrath because she'll punish you just like that. Fullish ball, outside off. McGrath steps out again and hammers it through covers for another boundary. 6 needed off 10 balls.

FOUR! Is that the game then? Full toss, on middle. Tahlia McGrath dances down the track and thumps it back over the bowler's head for a boundary. The youngster, Renuka Singh under immense pressure now.

Renuka Singh has been given the responsibility to bowl the penultimate over. Surprising tactics from Kaur. Normally you give the team's best bowler the 19th over, so that there are plenty of runs to defend in the final over. She has not bowled badly but considering that Renuka has debuted just a day ago, this is going to be massive pressure on her young shoulders
FOUR! What a shot from Georgia Wareham. Pitched up, around off. Wareham hangs back and absolutely creams this one over extra cover and picks up a boundary. 14 needed now off 12 balls.
Full and again this is drilled down the ground for a single.
Full and wide again, Wareham taps it to cover for one.

FOUR! Pandey goes for the wide yorker but ends up serving a half volley. Wareham drives it beautifully through cover-point and the fielder fails to cut it off in the deep. A welcome boundary for Australia Women.
Full and wide, play and a miss from Georgia Wareham.
A length ball, outside off. Tahlia McGrath fetches it and pulls it across towards deep mid-wicket for one. McGrath wants the second but won't get it.
Shikha Pandey (3-0-16-1) comes back on.
Flatter one, around off and kept out by Georgia Wareham. Rajeshwari Gayakwad ends her spell with figures of, 4-0-21-3. 25 needed off 18 balls.
Short and wide one, cut away to cover-point.
Georgia Wareham is the new batter in.

OUT! STUMPED! Another one bites the dust and Australia Women lose their sixth. Rajeshwari Gayakwad sees Nicola Carey dancing down the track and fires in a full and wide one. Carey can't get to it and ends up yorking herself. The keeper, Richa Ghosh fails to collect but the ball goes off her pads and back onto the stumps. Carey is stumped and Rajeshwari Gayakwad gets the breakthrough.
Commentary.Howout: st Richa Ghosh b Rajeshwari Gayakwad

Commentary.Commentary: Flighted ball, on off. McGrath uses her feet and eases it to long off for one.
FOUR! Smart batting from Tahlia McGrath. Outside off and McGrath shuffles right across her stumps and then sweeps it through square leg for a welcome boundary.

Close! Tossed up, on middle. Carey steps out and pushes it to mid-wicket. Carey takes off for a squick single and Shafali Verma has a shy at the stumps but misses. Carey survives and gets the single as well.
Full and outside off. Nicola Carey pushes it to extra cover for a single.
Length ball, on middle. Nicola Carey tucks it to mid-wicket.
Slower ball, on middle. Tahlia McGrath tucks it on the leg side. She crosses ends.
A low full toss on off, Nicola Carey pushes it to mid on for a run.
Fuller in length, on middle. Nicola Carey works it to long on for a couple of runs.
Length ball, on leg. Tahlia McGrath flicks it to deep square leg for one.
Renuka Singh (2-1-8-0) comes back into the attack.
Short and wide, outside off. Tahlia McGrath cuts it to sweeper cover for a single. 37 runs needed off 30 deliveries.
On middle, pushed back to the bowler again.
Loopy ball, on middle, pushed back to the bowler.
FOUR! Nicely played! Full and wide, outside off. Tahlia McGrath drives it through covers. Yastika Bhatia runs to her left from long off and dives but couldn't drag the ball back in. A boundary.
Short and outside off, Tahlia McGrath cuts it to point
On the pads, clipped to mid-wicket for a single.
Harmanpreet Kaur (1-0-3-1) brings herself back on.
On the pads, Tahlia McGrath tucks it on the leg side off the back foot. 43 needed from 36 balls.
Flatter and quicker, outside off. Tahlia McGrath guides it to point.
Short and on leg, worked to mid-wicket.
FOUR! Streaky! Short and outside off, Tahlia McGrath looks to cut. The ball goes off the outside edge and races away to the third man fence.
On middle, turned on the leg side for one.
Nicola Carey is in at number 7.

OUT! STUMPED! Gayakwad strikes! It is the crucial wicket of Beth Mooney this time. She was well set and could have taken Australia home. Rajeshwari Gayakwad bowls a flatter ball, outside off. The ball stays low a bit. Beth Mooney charges down the track and looks to swipe it across. The ball goes under her willow and Richa Ghosh does the rest behind the stumps. Half the side back in the hut now for Australia Women!
Commentary.Howout: st Richa Ghosh b Rajeshwari Gayakwad

Commentary.Commentary: Rajeshwari Gayakwad (2-0-10-1) comes back into the attack.
A single to end then! On imddle, this is worked towards mid-wicket for one.
On off, this is pushed through covers.
FOUR! Just wide of the fielder! On middle, Tahila comes down the track and hits it uppishly but just wide of the fielder at mid-wicket. Welcome boundary.
Mooney strokes this full ball through covers for one.
Outside off, this is guided to point.
Another chance? Not an easy one. On off, this is hit hard back towards the bowler. She gets a hand to it, the fielder at mid off, dives to her right and slows it down. Two taken.
Two leg byes! Short and on leg, Tahlia McGrath looks to pull but misses. She gets hit on the thigh pad and the ball rolls to fine leg. The batters sneak a couple of runs.
Outside off, Mooney drives it towards covers for a single.
Floats it up, outside off. Tahlia McGrath pushes it to mid off for a run.
Tosses it up, on middle. Tahlia McGrath pushes it back to the bowler.
Loopy ball, on off. Beth Mooney steps out and eases it down to long off for one.
Full and on off, driven to long off for a single.

NOT OUT! That is just short! Good length and outside off, Beth pushes at it, it goes off the outside edge. Lands just short of Ghosh who takes it and appeals. It is referred. Replays show that it lands just ahead.

The umpires have gone upstairs for a caught behind appeal. The ball might have just bounced in front of the keeper. The soft signal is Not Out and the replay confirms that the ball did bounce before Richa Ghosh pouched it. Beth Mooney survives.

Dropped! Tough chance though. Outside off, Tahlia McGrath looks to dirve, this goes off the outside edge, Ghosh dives to her right, gets a hand to it but spills it. That would have been a stunner. A single in the end.
A single as this is worked to mid-wicket.
A single as this is guided to point.
Outside off, this one stays low. Tahila looks to defend but this one stays low.
Good length and on off, defended.
Pooja Vastrakar (1-0-8-0) is back into the attack.
Another single as Tahila eases it down to long off.
On off, this is pushed to mid off for one.
Slower and on middle, defended.
FOUR! Mooney with another boundary to release the pressure! She sweeps and does so well, it is on the pads, she hits it in the fine leg region for a boundary,
On off, this is pushed down the ground to long off for one.
Tahlia McGrath comes in with her team in a spot of bother.

OUT! TAKEN! Perry now has to walk back and India well and truly in this one. The move to get on Sharma works wonders. That is a good catch. Perry comes down the track but gets a little too close to the pitch of the ball. She looks to loft it over covers but does not get the desired elevation. Kaur at covers, times her jump and takes a good catch.
Commentary.Howout: c Harmanpreet Kaur b Deepti Sharma

Commentary.Commentary: Deepti Sharma is inserted into the attack now.
FOUR! Welcome boundary! This is on the pads, it is swept through square leg. Races away to the fence. Spoils the over.
Perry comes down the track and eases it to long off for one.
Another run as this is pushed towards cover.
On middle, it is worked to mid-wicket.
Outside off, this is pushed to covers for one.
Flatter and on middle, this is worked down to long on for one.
Fired in, on off. Perry defends it out.
Ellyse Perry walks out to bat.

OUT! CAUGHT! The dangerous Ashleigh Gardner departs early. A half-tracker, way outside off and its there to be hit. Ashleigh Gardner goes a bit too hard at it and completely mistimes it. The ball goes to the left of the point fielder and Rajeshwari Gayakwad takes a sharp catch. Harmanpreet Kaur gets the breakthrough and Australia Women lose their third. This game is still alive and 81 runs are needed off 73 balls.
Commentary.Howout: c Rajeshwari Gayakwad b Harmanpreet Kaur

Commentary.Commentary: On middle and this is pulled to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Here comes the wrong 'un. On off and the ball just turns away sharply from the left-hander and keeps a bit low as well. Mooney misses it completely.
Flatter one, well outside off. Gardner cuts it to deep point and rotates the strike.
On the pads, Mooney works it to deep square leg for a single.
Harmanpreet Kaur to operate now.
Flighted agin, around off and nudged to point.
Flatter one this time, Gardner rocks back and cuts it to cover-point.
Tossed up, on off and pushed towards cover.
Ashleigh Gardner walks out to bat at No.4.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! The skipper departs. Nicely flighted ball, around off and this one grips a bit. Meg Lanning dances down the pitch looking to whack it but she's completely undone by the flight and ends up knicking it. Richa Ghosh takes the catch and also whips off the bails. Even if Lanning didn't knick it, she would have been stumped. Is this a turning point in the match?
Commentary.Howout: c Richa Ghosh b Rajeshwari Gayakwad

Commentary.Commentary: Tossed up, on middle. Mooney steps out and eases it to long on for one.
Short and wide, cut away off the back foot to sweeper cover for one.
Spin time! Rajeshwari Gayakwad to roll her arms now.
Pitched up, on off and pushed to mid off. Australia Women are 33/1 at the end of the Powerplay. 86 needed now in 84 balls.
FOUR! Short and wide, Mooney uppercuts it into the vacant backward point fence.

LEG BYE! The ball is doing all sorts of things out there. On off and the batter is unsure if the ball will move away or nip back in. This one nips in sharply and takes Lanning by surprise. The ball goes off her arms towards backward point and they get a leg bye.
On a length, around off and angled in. The ball just moves away sharply after pitching and Lanning is bamboozled.
Fullish ball, outside off. Lanning slashes at it but fails to connect.
FOUR! Meg Lanning is looking to counterattack as she looks to go big again. A length ball, on off and Lanning gets it off the leading edge, over mid off and the ball tickles away into the fence.
Good-length ball, angled into middle and leg. Lanning tucks it around the corner and gets a single.
Pooja Vastrakar comes into the attack. She replaces Renuka Singh.
WIDE! Pandey lookd to go full and wide, but this is a bit too wide. The umpire does signal a wide.
On middle and leg, Lanning tries to release the pressure by going big. Lanning manages to lift it over mid on and picks up a couple.
Length again, on off and nips back in. Lanning looks to defend but gets an inside edge back onto the pads.
PEACH! You can't play at that! Around off and this one nips back in sharply and cuts Lanning in half. The ball just goes over the top of off stump.
FOUR! The pressure is now somewhat released. Back of a length, around off. Meg Lanning goes on the back foot and gets it through the point region for a boundary.
A length ball, outside off. Lanning taps it to cover-point.
FOUR! Short ball, down leg. Beth Mooney pulls it behind square on the leg side for a boundary.
Full and on off, Beth Mooney heaves it towards cow corner. Yastika Bhatia runs from deep mid-wicket and cuts it off. Keeps it down to two.
On middle, worked to deep square leg off the back foot for one.
Good-length ball, on middle, curling back in. Meg Lanning looks to defend but misses. She gets hit on the pads. Renuka Singh appeals for an LBW but the umpire says no.
On a length, outside off. Beth Mooney dabs it down to third man. She crosses ends.
Good-length ball, outside off. Beth Mooney rocks back and looks to cut but misses.
Length ball, on middle. Beth Mooney looks to flick but gets a leading edge this time. Luckily for Mooney, it falls beyond the mid on fielder. A single is taken.
Back of a length, outside off, shaping away. Beth Mooney pushes it towards covers.
JAFFA! Good-length ball, on off, nipping away. Beth Mooney steps out and looks to flick but misses. The ball zips past the outside edge and carries through to the keeper.
Beautifully played! Full and on the pads, Meg Lanning flicks it towards deep mid-wicket only for a single.
Width on offer, outside off. Beth Mooney dabs it down to third man for a single.
Touch fuller, outside off. Meg Lanning guides it to third man for a single.
Terrific bowing from India Women! Length ball, outside off. Beth Mooney taps it to point. A maiden over from Renuka Singh.
Short of a length, outside off. Mooney punches it to extra cover.
Fuller in length, outside off. Mooney drives it to extra cover.
Full and on off, driven to mid off.
Length delivery, on off, angling away. Beth Mooney looks to drive but gets beaten.
Short of a length, outside off. Mooney pushes it to cover.
Renuka Singh to steam in from the opposite end.
Full and outside off, driven towards mid on. 4 runs and a wicket from the first over.
Short and wide, outside off. Meg Lanning cuts it to point.
On a good length, on off. Meg Lanning looks to defend but again gets an inside edge onto the pads. Shikha Pandey pleads for an LBW but the umpire is unmoved.
Fuller in length, outside off. Meg Lanning looks to drive but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
The skipper, Meg Lanning is in early, at number 3.

OUT! BOWLED! Shikha Pandey, you beauty! This is bowled on a good length, in the sixth stump channel. The ball comes back in sharply. Alyssa Healy gets cramped for room. The ball goes through her defense and disturbs the furniture behind her. There's pretty much nothing she can do, such was the beauty of that delivery. Shikha Pandey draws first blood and India Women are pumped up.
FOUR! Intent straightaway from Healy. Short ball, on middle. Healy stands tall and sends the ball sailing towards the deep mid-wicket area for a boundary. A solid start for Australia Women.
